To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
streptococcus‐induced anti‐IgGs are important in the pathogenesis of APSGN.
streptococcus IgG Fc receptor activity is a major factor in the development of anti‐Igd antibodies, glomerular deposition and glomerular injury in experimental post‐streptococccal glomeruloneprhitis.
streptococcocal IgG Fc receptor activity might be important for the development of acute poststreptozocal glomerulonephtis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the IgG Fc receptor of streptocococci in the pathogenesis of acute poststreptocooccal glomeronephritis.
the role of bacterial Fc receptors (FCR) in the pathogenesis of post‐streptococccal glomeruloneprhitis.
the possible role of streptococcol IgG Fc receptor (FcR) activity in triggering acute poststreptocoal glomeruloneprhitis (APSGN) in man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fc‐mediated activation of the immune system is a prerequisite for the development of APSGN.
FcR activity of streptococcci is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for triggering renal tissue damage in APSGN, but that it is a necessary condition.
FcR‐mediated IgG‐dependent activation of macrophages and other cells is a key factor in the pathogenesis of APSGN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FcR on GAS is an important virulence factor in human disease, since it induces the production of anti‐Igd and IgG, and the deposition of IgG on the glomeruli, which are the main events in the development of APSGN.
the streptococca FcR‐mediated glomerular Ig deposition and anti‐Ig formation in the rabbits is a phenomenon that is not unique for group A streptozocci.
the FcR activity in GAS strains, and not the M protein, is a major factor for the development of anti‐Igd and anti‐IgE antibodies and for the induction of IgG‐mediated renal tissue damage in rabbits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FcR activity of GAS is an important virulence factor that can be targeted for vaccine development.
